The delivery function is `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It is protected by `safeDialContext` and `ValidateURL`, which check for reserved internal IP addresses.

Outbound HTTP delivery executes in the `Post` function at `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, via `safeClient.Do(req)`.

`PostAsync` merely queues work that later invokes `Post`. SSRF protection runs at dial time through `safeDialContext` and `safeClient` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. URL validation that rejects reserved and private IPs lives in `internal/webhook/validate.go` under `ValidateURL`, `isReservedIP`, and `reservedCIDRs`.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` is the runtime guard that blocks internal address delivery and also defeats DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` enforces restrictions only during URL creation or updates.

Outbound HTTP delivery runs in `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` (`safeClient.Do`). `PostAsync` only queues work; workers still call `Post`. Connections go through `safeDialContext` in the same file, which resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs using `isReservedIP` / `reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, IPv6 ULA). That dial-time check is the SSRF guard, including against DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` applies the same private-IP rule when a webhook URL is configured.
